target: Today becomes a real timetable — hour-grid plan with a drawn lived trace, plus a time logger (still-happening and retroactive entries)

customReplacement.reason: SwiftUI-only surface composed entirely from AnchorTheme tokens, Card, Chip and the existing drawn-day materials.

contract.purpose: Anchor helps a person plan a realistic day, follow the current intention, and learn why the day lived differed from the day planned.
contract.purposeSource: PRODUCT.md; owner stated on 26 September 2026 that the product they wanted was 'a well sorted timetable and logger'
contract.canonicalPurpose: Anchor helps a person plan a realistic day, follow the current intention, and learn why the day lived differed from the day planned.
contract.driftNote: Owner scoped the change through structured options: hour-grid timetable, retroactive + in-the-moment logging, Today-only scope. History stays as-is.
contract.audience: The owner using an iPhone and Mac throughout an ordinary day.
contract.job: See the day on a true time axis, place or move entries by tapping open time, and record what actually happened — running or finished.
contract.thesis: The plan is a straight, quiet hour grid; the day that was actually lived is drawn beside it in the hand-wiggled trace material the rest of the app uses.
contract.system: Existing paper/charcoal, native SF type, Anchor spacing, hairline hour marks, card surfaces and state tints — no new tokens.
contract.signature: Two traces on one timetable: planned blocks on the grid, and a thin drawn wiggle in the gutter marking when work really happened.
contract.risk: A full-day grid reads denser than the old compact list; mitigated by faint hairlines, a working-day default window, and scroll-to-now on open.

projectCheck.command: swift build && swift test (234 core + 36 UI package tests pass, including TimetableLayout lane packing and logged-entry review evidence); DebugLocal macOS and iOS app builds succeed

critique.note: Fresh review of the new grid and log sheet renders: consistent tokens, honest states, lived trace reads as intended. Not carried forward — the surface changed.

audit.note: Checked against the drawn-day contract: hairlines stay quiet, accent marks only now/active work, completed and skipped states dim rather than disappear.

findings: Native SwiftUI review, not a browser rendering; phone-width catalog images use macOS controls.
Local Mac UI automation is environment-blocked on this machine (runner SIGKILL before bootstrap); the new grid+logging journey runs in the hosted native-review workflow.
Overlapping blocks share equal-width lanes within a cluster — deliberate, matching calendar conventions.

ownerFeedback.note: Owner selected the hour-grid timetable, both logging modes (retroactive + quick), and Today-only scope via structured scoping options on 26 September 2026.
